title: Active surveillance of adverse events after immunization (AEFI) from the Local Health Unitof Ferrara, Italy.
ehr_evidence: The tools used included an informatic platform, VigiFarmacoVax, and a mobile phone system.
summary: Active SMS-based surveillance study evaluating the reporting rate, characteristics, and severity of adverse events following immunization (AEFI) in young children in Ferrara, Italy.
key_findings: 1,494 consents and 983 SMS replies were obtained from parents.
561 AEFI reports were validated, comprising 1,248 adverse events.
99.5% of AEFI were classified as not serious.
Pyrexia was the most frequent adverse event (37.5%), followed by mood disorders (26.5%) and gastrointestinal disorders (12.5%).
population: children aged ≤ 2 years who received vaccinations per the regional calendar in Ferrara, Italy (March 2018 - May 2019)
limitations: impossibility of knowing the outcome of the adverse event at the time of reporting
lack of guarantee of equity in adhering to the study due to language and mobile phone requirements
potential confounding by increased vaccination coverage and mandatory law debate
